title: B2+ · L14 — Academic English intro
description: Leer y producir ingles academico basico: hedging, nominalizacion, voz impersonal, y estructuras formales.

questions.prompt: Escribes un ensayo universitario sobre nutricion e inmunidad.
questions.question: Which is more academic?
options: Scientists found that vitamin D helps a lot.
Recent findings suggest that vitamin D may play a significant role in immune regulation.
questions.explanation: Academic register combina cuatro marcas: (1) nominalizacion ('findings' en vez de 'scientists found'), (2) hedging obligatorio ('suggest', 'may' — nunca afirmar categoricamente), (3) lexico preciso y latino ('significant role', 'immune regulation' vs 'helps a lot'), (4) impersonalidad (no 'scientists' como sujeto emocional). Error hispano tipico: traducir directo 'ayuda mucho' — vago y coloquial. Registro: aplica a papers, ensayos universitarios, y grants — no a divulgacion cientifica popular.
examples: The evidence indicates a potential correlation between screen time and sleep disruption. → hedge triple
Preliminary data appear to support the hypothesis, though further study is warranted. → cautela + reserva

questions.prompt: Tu tutora te dice que uses mas 'nominalization' en tu paper.
questions.question: 'Nominalization' means turning verbs and adjectives into:
questions.explanation: Nominalizacion = convertir verbos y adjetivos en sustantivos. Es LA marca #1 del estilo academico anglo. Ejemplos: 'we investigated' -> 'the investigation'; 'reduce' -> 'reduction'; 'complex' -> 'complexity'. Efectos: (1) prosa mas densa (mas informacion por palabra), (2) tono impersonal (elimina el actor humano), (3) permite cadenas nominales complejas. OJO: excesiva nominalizacion produce prosa 'zombie' (Steven Pinker) — mata claridad. Balance: academico si, monstruo nominal no.
examples: Verb: We analyzed → Noun: The analysis revealed... → academic conversion clasica
Verb: They implemented → Noun: The implementation of X led to Y. → chain nominal

questions.statement: Academic writing prefers absolute claims like 'proves' and 'always' over hedged claims like 'suggests' and 'often'.
questions.explanation: FALSO — es al reves. Hedging academico es esencial y obligatorio en la mayoria de disciplinas cientificas. 'Proves', 'always', 'never' son casi tabu — la ciencia raramente prueba absolutos (Popper: solo se refutan hipotesis, no se prueban); usar absolutos delata autor amateur o descuidado. 'Suggests', 'tends to', 'may', 'appears to' son standard. Verbos hedge esenciales: suggest, indicate, appear, tend to, seem to. Modales hedge: may, might, could. Error hispano cultural: la tradicion academica hispana permite mas confianza retorica; en anglo la modestia epistemica es virtud.
examples: Weak: This proves the theory. → tono ingenuo/amateur
Strong: These results are consistent with the theory. → hedging pro

questions.prompt: Conectas dos argumentos en tu tesis. El primero era una premisa, el segundo la evidencia.
questions.question: Which is the most academic transition?
questions.explanation: Connectores academicos formales: FURTHERMORE, MOREOVER, IN ADDITION, NOTABLY, CONSEQUENTLY, THUS, HENCE, HOWEVER, NEVERTHELESS. Cortos casuales ('so', 'also', 'plus', 'and') estan prohibidos al inicio de oracion academica. 'Data indicate' (plural latino, con verbo plural — 'data are/indicate' es tecnicamente correcto en academic aunque 'data is' se acepta ampliamente ahora). Registro: distinguir estos connectores es senal de dominio del genero. Error hispano frecuente: usar 'also' o 'so' al inicio, delata registro semi-informal.
examples: Moreover, previous studies corroborate this finding across three continents.
Notably, the effect was more pronounced in the control group. → 'notably' anticipa insight

questions.text: The results appear to support the hypothesis, although further research is warranted before drawing definitive conclusions.
questions.explanation: Frase academica prototipica del discussion section. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'appear to' con /pɪətə/; 'is warranted' con /zw/ /ɪzˈwɒrəntɪd/; 'drawing definitive' con /ŋd/ /ˈdrɔːɪŋdɪˈfɪnətɪv/. Colocaciones academicas fundamentales: 'appear to support' (parece apoyar — hedge doble: 'appear' + evidencia indirecta), 'further research is warranted' (colocacion cristalizada — se necesita mas investigacion), 'drawing definitive conclusions' (llegar a conclusiones definitivas — colocacion fija). Registro: paper / thesis obligatorio.
examples: The findings appear to corroborate previous work in this area.
Further investigation is warranted to establish causality. → 'establish causality' colocacion clave

questions.prompt: Introduces una afirmacion en tu ensayo sin adjudicarsela a un autor especifico.
questions.question: In academic English, 'it is argued that' is used to:
options: Introduce a claim impersonally without direct attribution.
questions.explanation: 'It is argued that' es passive impersonal estandar del genero academico. Funciones: (1) distancia al autor de la afirmacion (proteccion retorica), (2) sugiere consenso o multiples autores sin citar todos, (3) permite introducir claim a discutir despues. Muy comun en essays y literature reviews. Alternativas equivalentes: 'It has been proposed that', 'It is widely held that', 'It is generally accepted that'. Registro: humanidades y social sciences lo usan mas que ciencias duras. OJO: usado en exceso suena evasivo.
examples: It is widely argued that inflation targeting has succeeded in most advanced economies.
It has been proposed that consciousness emerges from complexity. → 'proposed' variante

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de vocabulario academico con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Seis terminos indispensables del vocabulario academico anglo. 'Peer-reviewed' es sello de credibilidad cientifica — sistema que valida un paper antes de publicacion. 'Longitudinal study' = seguimiento de los mismos sujetos en el tiempo (vs 'cross-sectional' = snapshot en un momento). 'Findings' es plural obligatorio en academico (no 'finding' salvo un descubrimiento unico). 'Methodology' se distingue de 'methods' — methodology es el marco teorico, methods son las tecnicas concretas. Error hispano frecuente: usarlos intercambiablemente.
examples: The paper is peer-reviewed and has been widely cited over the past decade.
A longitudinal study over 20 years revealed a clear pattern of decline. → design fuerte

questions.target: This paper examines the extent to which digital literacy correlates with civic engagement among young adults in urban settings.
questions.explanation: Frase abstract academico impecable. Estructura: (1) verbo activo academico ('examines'), (2) construction magica 'the extent to which' (el grado en que — permite matiz cuantitativo), (3) verbo relacional ('correlates with') que no compromete causalidad, (4) delimitacion demografica ('young adults, urban settings'). 'Civic engagement' es colocacion academica precisa (participacion civica). Ritmo natural: tono neutral y firme, sin dramatismo, sin contracciones (academic spoken tampoco las usa). Ritmo lento, silabas claras. Registro: abstract / opening paragraph.
examples: This study investigates the relationship between sleep patterns and academic performance in undergraduates.
The research explores how remote work has reshaped organizational culture post-pandemic.

questions.prompt: Reportas tu metodologia en el methods section.
questions.question: Which is the most academic way to say 'we did an experiment'?
questions.explanation: Voz pasiva impersonal es la marca #1 de academic writing en muchas disciplinas cientificas (STEM especialmente). 'An experiment was conducted' vs 'we did an experiment' — la pasiva focaliza el METODO, no al autor humano (objetividad cientifica). Verbo tecnico 'conducted' vs coloquial 'did'. Reglas de la American Psychological Association (APA): passive apropiada cuando el actor es irrelevante o obvio. Diferencia disciplinar: STEM prefiere pasiva; social sciences y humanities modernos aceptan mas 'we'. Registro: universal en methods sections.
examples: A survey was administered to 500 participants over a six-week period.
The samples were analyzed using mass spectrometry. → passive + tecnica

questions.statement: In academic English, using first-person 'I' or 'we' is now widely accepted in many fields.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Tendencia moderna documentada: muchas revistas top (Nature, Science, Cell) ahora aceptan e incluso recomiendan 'we found', 'we hypothesized' — mejora la claridad y reconoce la agencia investigadora. La regla vieja de 'nunca uses I/we' era exceso victoriano. Diferencias disciplinares: STEM modernos aceptan; algunas humanidades juridicas y ciertas revistas europeas conservadoras mantienen impersonal. Regla practica actual: verifica el style guide de la revista objetivo. Error hispano academico: seguir la regla antigua rigidamente cuando la revista permite primera persona.
examples: We hypothesized that... → aceptado en Nature/Science modernos
We argue that... → comun en social science papers actuales

questions.prompt: Necesitas afirmar que un tema esta bien documentado en la literatura.
questions.question: Which sentence has the strongest academic register?
options: A substantial body of literature substantiates this claim.
questions.explanation: 'A substantial body of literature substantiates this claim' contiene CINCO marcas academicas: (1) 'substantial body of literature' — colocacion academica cristalizada; (2) 'substantiates' — verbo latino preciso (respalda con evidencia); (3) hedge implicito 'body of literature' (colectivo, no absoluto); (4) formalidad de vocabulario; (5) nominalizacion ('claim'). 'Lots of studies show' es informal y vago. 'Everyone knows' es falacia ad populum. Registro: literature review section o argument academico. Colocacion nativa: prefiere 'a growing body' (creciente) o 'a substantial body' (sustancial).
examples: A growing body of evidence supports the intervention across diverse populations.
The literature is largely consistent on this point, though methodological differences persist.

questions.text: The findings should be interpreted with caution given the limitations of the sample size.
questions.explanation: Formula estandar de la 'limitations section' — obligatoria en todo paper serio. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'should be' con weak /ʃədbi/; 'interpreted with' con catenacion /ɪnˈtɜːprɪtɪdwɪð/; 'given the' con weak /ɡɪvnðə/. Colocaciones academicas: 'interpreted with caution' (interpretar con cautela — colocacion fija), 'given the limitations' (dado que hay limitaciones — construccion academica formal), 'sample size' (tamano de muestra — no 'sample size number' que seria calco). Muestra rigor academico y humildad epistemica.
examples: These results should be interpreted with caution due to methodological constraints.
The findings must be considered in light of several limitations. → 'in light of' colocacion pro

questions.prompt: Estudias estadistica y tu profesor repite este mantra.
questions.question: 'Correlation does not imply causation' is:
options: A fundamental principle of scientific reasoning.
questions.explanation: Principio central de razonamiento cientifico y estadistico. Aunque X y Y varien conjuntamente (correlacion), uno no necesariamente CAUSA el otro — podria haber (1) variable oculta que causa ambas, (2) causalidad inversa, (3) coincidencia. Ejemplo famoso: ventas de helado correlacionan con ahogamientos (variable oculta: verano). Frase esencial en academic argument moderno — cita obligada en cualquier discusion sobre estudios observacionales. Solo experimentos controlados (RCTs) permiten establecer causalidad con confianza. Registro: cientifico universal.
examples: While correlation is strong, causation cannot be established without experimental design.
The two variables move together, but this does not imply direct causation. → hedge cautelar

questions.statement: 'Notwithstanding' is a formal academic connector meaning 'despite'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Notwithstanding' = 'despite' pero registro ULTRA FORMAL. Se ve en juridicos, academicos, policy papers, y contratos. Estructura curiosa: proviene de 'not-with-standing' (literalmente 'no oponiendo') — construccion cristalizada del ingles medio. Puede ir antes o despues del sustantivo ('notwithstanding the criticism' o 'the criticism notwithstanding'). Alternativas academicas de mismo registro: 'in spite of', 'regardless of'. En speaking academico se usa poco (demasiado pesado); en writing academico es apropiado. Registro: legal, academic, policy.
examples: Notwithstanding these limitations, the study contributes meaningfully to the field.
The reform was passed, notwithstanding significant opposition from opposition parties. → posposicion

questions.target: In conclusion, while the evidence is compelling, additional longitudinal research is needed to establish causality with confidence.
questions.explanation: Cierre academico prototipico de discussion o conclusion section. Estructura: (1) marker de conclusion ('in conclusion'), (2) reconocimiento del hallazgo ('while the evidence is compelling'), (3) reserva epistemica obligatoria ('additional longitudinal research is needed'), (4) meta cientifica ('establish causality with confidence'). Ritmo natural: tono firme y neutral, sin dramatismo, sin contracciones, pausas marcadas tras 'conclusion,' y 'compelling,'. 'Compelling' es adjetivo academico pulido (convincente). 'With confidence' hedge final que suaviza la aspiracion causal.
examples: In conclusion, the data offer strong preliminary support, though replication is essential.
To summarize, our findings warrant further investigation across broader populations. → alt cierre
